s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass enlargement over the past four months
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
Well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass on soft-tissue ultrasound
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Painless right vulvar mass
Mass first noted two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
No pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Hypertension managed with valsartan/amlodipine
Hysterectomy in 2016 for abnormal uterine bleeding
Post-menopausal
No history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam unremarkable
12cm, non-tender mass of the right labia majora
No erythema, lymphadenopathy, or signs of inflammation
Pelvic exam otherwise normal
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging
Routine laboratory results within normal limits
